Latin superstar Karol G is known for a lot of things, namely her infectious music and her bright, bubbly personality. She’s also a beauty icon in her own right, with millions of fans constantly clamoring for her beauty secrets. Now, her esthetician, Flavia Lanini, is spilling the tea on how she helps keep the glow going while on tour with the singer. Her secret? Kiss New York’s K-Beauty skincare collection. “I first tried the Kiss New York skincare products myself and loved them, and was so excited to incorporate them into Karol’s skin prep,” she shared. So, which products does she use to keep La Bichota’s skin bright and hydrated while on tour? She breaks it down below. First, she treats the skin: “I started by prepping her skin with the [Kiss New York Bright Vita Charge Toner Pad],” said Lanini. “They add hydration after cleansing, which helps make the skin feel smooth and ready for the next steps. I also chose them because the niacinamide and glutathione help brighten the skin, fade the look of dark spots and create a more even complexion.” Next comes a facial massage — with a little bit of help. “I used [the Radiant Glow Vita Capsule Cream] during her facial massage to give the skin hydration and a beautiful glow,” she shared. “I love the dual texture. This cream has a clear gel that helps deeply plump the skin and then yellow capsules that boost radiance as I massage them together. It also helps to reduce dark spots and quickly repair the skin barrier, leaving the complexion brighter and with a glass skin finish. The clear gel also contains wrinkle-tightening ingredients and four types of peptides to support hydration.” “After the massage, I gently removed some of the remaining product and went over the skin again with the toner pad,” she adds. “Since the pads are dual-sided, I can switch between the textured side and the smooth side to refine the texture and add extra moisture.” To lock everything in, Lanini opts for the Pure Glow Vita Bright Moisturizer. “I applied this to finish, hydrate and leave the skin looking fresh and luminous. Brightening is the goal through this whole routine, so I want every step to build on the one before,” she stated. ”This cream gives an instant, natural tone-up effect that makes the skin look brighter, smoother and more illuminated, while also giving deep hydration and soothing barrier care. This all thanks to the formula’s niacinamide, Vitamin C and 7-Superfood Complex (Sea Buckthorn, Carrot, Guava, and more)." Lastly, it’s time for one more dose of moisture. “I finished the treatment with the PDRN hydrogel mask for an extra boost of hydration and glow,” Lanini shared. ”This is the perfect last step because the product name describes exactly the result you would want from an at-home treatment. As this jelly mask melts into the skin, it will help to create a poreless and reflective glow." The result? A soothed and hydrated “glass-skin-like” base ready to help bring the Tropitour’s showstopping glam to life, courtesy of Karol G’s makeup artist, Duvan Foronda. title: The 5 Best ASUS Routers of 2026 - rtings.com
content: Few brands cast as wide a net in the world of Wi-Fi as ASUS. From their gamer-geared ROG and TUF lineups to the sleek ZenWiFi mesh family, the best router for you depends on what problem you're trying to solve. While this variety is a major plus for consumer choice, the sheer number of options available can certainly make finding the right one feel overwhelming. We've tested over 80 of the most popular routers, including over 15 ASUS routers (with more on the way). Below, you'll find our breakdown of the best ASUS routers on the market, chosen for their performance, features, and overall value. For more recommendations, check out our guides to the best gaming routers, the best long-range routers, and the best routers overall. Since we started reviewing them in 2024, we've tested over 60 routers. We maintain complete editorial independence and impartiality by purchasing each router ourselves, which ensures we aren't testing specially selected review units. Rather than casually assessing performance by throwing on Netflix and seeing if it works, we rigorously evaluate each router on a standardized testing platform, providing you with all the data you need to compare different models. If you're after the absolute best ASUS router we've tested, look no further than the ASUS ZenWiFi BT10. This flagship Wi-Fi 7 mesh system is a fantastic choice if you live in a larger home, have multiple floors, or find that the coverage from a standalone router simply isn't cutting it. The two-pack variant we tested includes a companion node for added range, but the BT10 can also operate as a standalone if you don't need a multi-node mesh. Performance takes center stage here, with this router boasting the highest speed and range scores out of any ASUS device we've tested. Power users will be pleased with its solid mix of two 10Gbps ports, one 1Gbps port, and support for multi-WAN failover; it's ideal for ultra-fast fiber and Wi-Fi 7 devices, though its port selection is ultimately lighter than the generously equipped ASUS ROG Strix GS-BE18000 (more on that below). Specs aside, each node is sleek and low-profile, making it far easier to position around the home than some of the company's more angular designs from its 'gaming' entries. That convenience makes a difference, given that open placement is essential for achieving the best range and speed from a mesh system. Looking for more mesh router recommendations? We've got you covered. If you don't need a dedicated mesh or simply want a massive selection of Ethernet ports, we recommend the ASUS ROG Strix GS-BE18000 as the best ASUS router in the upper mid-range category. It's the best-performing Wi-Fi 7 standalone we've tested from the brand, making it an attractive option regardless of whether you plan to game. While its rugged styling obviously caters to gamers, the real draw comes from its combination of exceptional range, high-speed performance, and a stacked selection of multi-gigabit Ethernet ports that easily beat others in this class. Notably, this router includes Automated Frequency Coordination (AFC) support to boost its 6GHz band's power and range, though this benefit only matters if you have Wi-Fi 6E or 7 devices (and live in a region that supports it). While this tri-band router's 2.5Gbps WAN port falls short of the ASUS ZenWiFi BT10's massive 10Gbps ceiling, it counters with a formidable array of seven 2.5Gbps LAN ports on the rear. If you're running multiple gaming consoles, PCs, or even a Network-Attached Storage (NAS) solution at home, you'd be hard-pressed to find a more cost-effective hub for a high-speed wired ecosystem (for example, the TP-Link Archer BE900 offers a similar number of high-speed ports, but costs nearly twice as much). Two of its ports are even designated "gaming ports"; in practice, this just means the router will supposedly prioritize traffic for whatever devices you connect to them. If the above options are outside your budget (or simply overpowered for your usage), we recommend the ASUS TUF Gaming BE9400 as one of the best ASUS routers at a mid-range price. Like our premium picks, this is still a tri-band Wi-Fi 7 router with 2.4GHz, 5GHz, and 6GHz bands, though it's best approached as a stellar general-use option rather than a niche gaming tool. While its tactical styling might not be to everyone's taste, it serves as a great example of what we found when looking at Wi-Fi latency and why gaming routers aren't inherently better: marketing aside, real-world performance comes down to what's under the hood. Thankfully, this router delivers exactly where it counts, all at a more competitive price. It maintains excellent speeds, strong coverage, and a great selection of multi-gigabit ports. While its chassis isn't particularly tailored to tight spaces, six adjustable antennas offer some flexibility in its positioning. More interestingly, this TUF router delivers lower wireless latency than almost any other router we've tested. That's a meaningful advantage if you often game over Wi-Fi, though it doesn't change the bigger picture: Ethernet is king for competitive gaming. While you don't get the same seven-port selection as the ASUS ROG Strix GS-BE18000 (or the refined design of the ASUS ZenWiFi BT10), this router still offers a respectable selection of three 2.5Gbps ports, leaving little room for complaint at this price. For a more budget-conscious entry into the latest wireless standard, we recommend the ASUS RT-BE92U as the best lower mid-range ASUS router. It sits on the pricier side of the lower-mid tier, but that's par for the course with ASUS's generally elevated price floor. Despite its positioning in the market, this router offers astonishingly high 6GHz peak speeds and respectable range for small to medium-sized homes. While its standalone coverage leaves something to be desired, the model includes AiMesh support as a means to extend your range with compatible devices. An upright, angular design, coupled with four prominent antennas and a red racing stripe down the middle, gives this router a distinct "gamer" aesthetic, despite a lack of heavy marketing as such. Regardless, it's a highly capable mid-tier entry from ASUS and a cost-effective way to get your Wi-Fi 6E and 7 devices onto the 6GHz band (with unbeatable speeds for the price). If you want a straightforward, low-cost option and don't need cutting-edge Wi-Fi 7 technology, the ASUS RT-AX1800S is our top no-frills budget pick. As a dual-band Wi-Fi 6 router, it predates support for the faster 6GHz band. Even so, its hardware packs in plenty of utility for everyday users (learn more about the differences between Wi-Fi standards in our comparison article). Its defining strength lies in its value; a standard 1Gbps WAN port paired with a surprisingly generous selection of five 1Gbps LAN ports makes this router more than sufficient for sub-gigabit internet plans. For a highly accessible price, it delivers reliable performance for basic web browsing, streaming, smart home tech, and simultaneous connections around the home. Naturally, that lower price tag means accepting a few trade-offs: the router's wireless range is limited, making it ill-suited to sprawling layouts, and a lack of multi-gigabit support caps its utility for any higher-speed internet plans. It isn't built to deliver the low latency or raw speeds required for power users or competitive gamers, but it's more than sufficient for everyday use and 4k streaming, even across multiple devices. That said, if your home is full of modern Wi-Fi 6E or 7 hardware (or if you just need a bit more headroom in the bandwidth department), stepping up to any of the recommendations above is well worth the investment. ASUS routers generally offer deep customization options through the ASUSWRT web interface and ASUS Router app. A big plus if you're the type to tinker, or simply want a higher degree of control over your network security. Unlike many competing router brands, ASUS doesn't lock common features behind a monthly subscription model. Features like parental controls, security tools, QoS, and VPN support are generally available without an ongoing fee. ASUS's higher-end routers and ZenWiFi mesh systems consistently deliver some of the strongest speed and range results we've seen from the brand. Many ASUS routers include a generous selection of multi-gigabit Ethernet ports. This is useful if you have wired devices such as a gaming PC or console, a NAS, a desktop workstation, or a home server. ASUS routers don't always deliver the best price-to-performance ratio; some competing brands offer similar or better performance for less, especially in the budget and mid-range categories. ASUS gives users plenty of control, but that depth can also make its software feel less intuitive at first. If you're after a plug-and-play setup with minimal configuration, you might find alternatives from other brands more appealing. TP-Link and ASUS both offer an extensive portfolio of routers, from budget models to powerful flagships. TP-Link is generally more competitive on performance per dollar in the mid-range space, while ASUS's deep network controls and configurability offer outstanding value to tinkerers, gamers, and enthusiasts. Crucially, the value of TP-Link's latest offerings has been undercut by subscription models that lock some security settings, QoS features, and parental controls behind a monthly subscription. This is a practice that's becoming increasingly common in the industry, but ASUS has yet to adopt it. ASUS and eero take vastly different approaches to home networking. Eero's specialty is simplicity, with a clean, app-based ecosystem and polished user interface for effortless operation out of the box. ASUS offers far more control over your network through its app and web interface, with the ZenWiFi lineup being the closest direct competitor to eero's whole-home mesh solutions. Much like TP-Link, eero's advanced networking tools are locked behind a monthly subscription model, while ASUS includes comparable features at no additional cost. ASUS and NETGEAR are both prominent brands in the home networking space, but they appeal to different user needs. ASUS routers prioritize flexibility and granular control, with AiMesh technology that lets you mix and match compatible ASUS devices to build a mesh network. NETGEAR focuses on a more streamlined setup experience, but requires a recurring subscription for full access to security tools and QoS settings, in line with competitors. Additionally, some of NETGEAR's "Wi Fi 7" routers omit core generation features like Multi-Link Operation (MLO), making it important to verify specific hardware capabilities before buying. ASUS routers offer a mix of solid performance and flexible controls for users looking to get the most out of their internet plan. Features like mesh support, parental controls, and useful security tools are included across lineups and don't require a monthly subscription to access. While certain consumer lineups lean heavily into gaming-focused branding (such as ROG and TUF), the brand's consistent performance across a variety of price points makes ASUS a strong contender for most households, not just gamers. ZenWiFi: ASUS's flagship mesh series. These routers are generally sold in multi-pack systems and are designed to provide broader, more consistent whole-home coverage than a conventional standalone. Built around a simplistic app-based setup and a sleek, antenna-free aesthetic, ZenWiFi systems don't require a monthly subscription and also support AiMesh, so you can expand your network further with compatible devices. ROG (Republic of Gamers): The ROG lineup consists of ASUS's high-end standalone routers, marketed heavily towards gamers and enthusiasts. These models typically feature aggressive styling, a strong selection of multi-gigabit ports, and gaming-focused software features like traffic prioritization and dedicated 'gaming' ports. TUF Gaming: TUF Gaming routers are ASUS's more budget-focused gaming models, aiming to provide the same essential hardware features for power users at a more accessible price. TUF routers usually ship with a less expansive set of software tools, cutting out some extra features in favor of strong conventional performance and value. RT Series: ASUS' traditional RT lineup covers everything from entry-level home routers to premium standalone units. These routers cater to standard households, smart homes, and general users who want ASUS' signature network flexibility without gaming-specific branding. Most RT models still include ASUS' core software features, such as AiMesh support, parental controls, and more advanced networking settings. title: Karol G’s “Viajando Por El Mundo” Is Taking Over NYC — Here’s Everything to Know - Remezcla
content: Ahead of Karol G’s Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour taking over MetLife Stadium, the “Viajando Por El Mundo” pop-up, powered by Cash App, who is the official tour partner, is taking over High Line Nine Gallery in Chelsea for two days on September 17 and 18. Giving fans another way to pregame before heading out to see La Bichota onstage or, if you didn’t score tickets, a way to feel close to the Colombian star’s Tropicoqueta era. Named after the song from her fifth album, Tropicoqueta, the “Viajando Por El Mundo” pop-up lets fans imagine visiting all the places she sings about in the track without booking a flight. The pop-up debuted in Los Angeles and recently stopped in El Paso, and will next head to Miami and Dallas, tied to Karol G’s concerts in each city. And now it’s New York’s turn to enjoy. So, what exactly can you expect? The experience includes getting your passport stamped to enter different installations and photo moments. You can grab a slice of pizza inspired by the lyric about eating pizza in New York, step into a tequila-filled Mexican experience, and take a shot of Karol G’s 200 Copas by Casa Dragones. Channel your inner romantic in a Paris setup featuring the Eiffel Tower. There’s also a Las Vegas-inspired moment nodding to the song’s spontaneous wedding lyric, and a final photo op that transports you to Italy with a Vespa and the Leaning Tower of Pisa. Also, it wouldn’t be a pop-up without some merch to take home, and the Cash App-powered storefront includes a limited-edition T-shirt inspired by the song’s lyrics and destinations. Cash App Card holders get an extra perk: 20% off merch purchases at the pop-up, so if that T-shirt has your name all over it, you’ll want that card ready. The experience is designed to be interactive, so whether you’re going for the photo or video ops to share on social, the merch, the Karol G content, or simply because you’re already in the neighborhood, there’s plenty to see. The pop-up will be open to the public on Thursday, Sept. 17, from 11 a.m. to 6 p.m. ET and Friday, Sept. 18, from 11 a.m. to 6 p.m. ET at High Line Nine Gallery, located at 507 W. 27th St. in New York City. title: Will Higher Costs and Softer FICC Weigh on Goldman Q3 Momentum? - TradingView
content: The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc.’s GS third-quarter 2026 outlook suggests some pressure on Global Banking & Markets performance, as softer fixed-income trading and higher expenses could partly offset continued strength in investment banking (IB). Speaking at the Barclays 24th Annual Global Financial Services Conference on Sept. 16, CEO David Solomon pointed to relatively softer activity in fixed income, currencies and commodities (FICC), while broader client engagement and capital-markets activity remained constructive. However, Solomon noted that equity trading has been very strong in the third quarter. The moderation in FICC follows a strong first half of 2026. Goldman generated $6.24 billion in IB fees during the period, up 52% year over year, supported by robust advisory and underwriting activity. FICC revenues totaled $8.60 billion, rising 9%, while Global Banking & Markets revenues climbed 35% year over year to $28.26 billion. The softer FICC backdrop is worth watching because trading remains a key contributor to Goldman’s Global Banking & Markets revenues and provides earnings diversification, alongside investment-banking fees. Therefore, weaker fixed-income trading in the third quarter could reduce the incremental revenue support from Markets, though continued strength in equities should provide a partial cushion, even as advisory, M&A and underwriting activity remains healthy. At the same time, rising operating costs could limit the extent to which strong deal activity translates into earnings growth. At the conference, Solomon indicated that expenses are running higher amid elevated transaction volumes and accelerated technology investments. Non-compensation expenses are expected to increase by more than $500 million sequentially in the third quarter of 2026. Overall, softer FICC activity and a sequential increase in non-compensation expenses could dent Goldman’s third-quarter earnings momentum by limiting the benefits from strong revenue trends. However, the impacts may be partly cushioned by robust equity trading, a healthy IB fee backlog, and sustained advisory and underwriting activity. Thus, while higher costs and weaker fixed-income trading could pressure near-term earnings growth, continued strength across IB and equities should help prevent a sharper slowdown. Other banks that provided updated outlooks include Citigroup C and KeyCorp KEY. Citigroup’s third-quarter outlook appears relatively upbeat. Management expects markets revenues to grow in the mid-single digits year over year, supported by equities, financing and foreign exchange. Citigroup also projects IB revenues to increase in the low-single digits, with further upside possible if pending transactions close before the quarter-end. KeyCorp has come up with an updated 2026 outlook, with revenues projected to rise 8% year over year. Previously, the company targeted revenues to rise 7-8%. The increase is driven by higher non-interest income, which is expected to grow 4-5% (up from the prior mentioned 3-4% increase). KeyCorp anticipates net interest income to rise 9-11%. Goldman’s Price Performance, Valuation, & Estimates GS shares have jumped 16.6% in the past year compared with the industry’s growth of 12.6%. From a valuation standpoint, Goldman trades at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 13.16X, above the industry’s average of 13.43X. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for GS’s 2026 and 2027 earnings implies year-over-year rallies of 34.2% and 4.9%, respectively. Estimates for both years have been unchanged over the past month. title: Kenny G’s sax to serenade Flagstar at Westbury Music Fair - LI Press
content: The sweet, smooth soprano saxophone sound of Kenny G has enchanted audiences since he stepped into the spotlight with his breakthrough 1986 album, Duotones. His sixth studio album, Breathless (1992), became the bestselling instrumental album ever. Miracles (1994), his first holiday album, sold over 13 million copies, making it the most successful Christmas album to date. He has become one of the best-selling artists of all time and the best-selling instrumentalist in history. Kenny G, born Kenneth Bruce Gorelick on June 5, 1956, has collaborated with a long list of high-profile artists including Aretha Franklin, The Weeknd, Andrea Bocelli, and Kanye West. In November 2025, he made a special cameo appearance in A Very Jonas Christmas Movie, playing a soprano saxophone solo alongside Nick, Joe and Kevin Jonas on the single he co-wrote, “Coming Home This Christmas.” He teamed up with Charlie Puth on Puth’s song “Cry” and followed that up by accompanying Puth with his soprano saxophone at the Super Bowl LX for a performance of “The Star-Spangled Banner.” In his 2025 memoir Life in the Key of G, co-written with Philip Lerman, the musician shared that he was inspired to play the saxophone by watching The Ed Sullivan Show. “I was 10 years old when I picked up the saxophone and I still love playing it,” he said. In his early career, he played in funk bands and backed up artists including Barry White and Liberace. He’s been married and divorced twice and prefers to keep his current relationship private, though digital network creator Katina Ann has shared posts and photos of them together. “I don’t like my personal life to be part of anything that I discuss publicly and that’s only because no one’s that interested,” he said. “I know a lot of celebrities that everyone wants to know everything about, but when I go to my local grocery store there’s no frenzy at all and I’m not complaining.” Like a scientist in his laboratory, Kenny G is always brewing up another musical gem in his studio, conveniently located on the grounds of his LA estate. “There’s a small saxophone part I’m doing for something I can’t tell you about, but I want to make it perfect and it’s literally five seconds of me playing two different times,” he said of his current project. “It will probably take me two hours to get it exactly the way I want it. Obviously it could take me five minutes to do it, but I know myself. I’m going to carve out about three or four hours in my studio today and I’m not going to leave until I get that part done. So that’s a lot of work, but it’s going to be fun.” Kenny G is still enthusiastic about composing and playing his signature saxophone. “I practice three hours every day, usually from 6 a.m. to 9 a.m. so I can be at my top,” he said. “That’s what keeps me excited. Every day I’m trying to get better. Every show I play, I want it to be a better show. I’m completely motivated to play my best show.” It was a pleasure to speak with Kenny G before the start of his tour, which lands at Flagstar at Westbury Music Fair on Sept. 26. What about Flagstar at Westbury Music Fair keeps you going back? It’s fun to go back to places we’ve been before. It’s in the round, so that’s not necessarily something that you do very often. It’s a fun place to watch a concert, because nobody really has the advantage since the stage revolves. At some point, you’re going to be right in the front row of it no matter where you are. How did your collaboration with Puth on his song “Cry” come about? He called me and I listened to the song and liked it. That’s all it took for me to do it. I knew who he was, but that didn’t matter. It was the tune that mattered. If it’s a song I like and I feel I can play well on, then I’ll do it. It was easy to play and it was fun. Did it take you only an hour to compose your solo part on “Cry”? Something like that. I didn’t want to get too far into it without him giving me some feedback. So, I took about an hour and then sent it back to him to see if he liked what I did. Then I took the next few hours to fine-tune it. What stands out to you about accompanying Puth on “The Star-Spangled Banner” at Super Bowl XL last February? It was pretty exciting. Everybody wants to be there and you’ve got a backstage pass. It happened fast. There’s a lot of prep work for the two minutes that it takes to do it and it was really fun. I liked playing my little sax parts to go around his vocals. It was really his gig and he was generous to share it with me. How do you decide which artists you will collaborate with? It depends on the vibe of the artist and the song. It’s never about the money. I didn’t get paid for doing the thing with Charlie. I don’t usually charge for solos. It depends on the music and the artist. Why did you decide to bring in Lerman as a co-writer on your memoir, Life in the Key of G? I liked his demo. It was kind of funny and smart. Then I talked to him on the phone and we seemed to have a lot in common. We were about the same age, the same kind of background. The hard part with Phil was him understanding how I make things funny, because he has his own way of making things funny. We had a learning curve on him getting my vibe and then it just worked. You are in the Guinness Book of World Records: 1997 for playing the longest note held on the saxophone using circular breathing. What is circular breathing? I’ll be doing it in the show at Westbury. It’s holding a note for a long time and you breathe at the same time. You don’t stop playing the note to take a breath. It’s a technique that wind instrument players do. Maybe do a duet with Paul McCartney, but I don’t know him. I would never reach out to him. It would have to come from him that he’s doing something and thinks my sound might work for him. That would be great. Maybe be part of a really amazing film score. My wish list would be that somebody like Ron Howard or Steven Spielberg would call me and say give me a theme song for my movie. Is there anything else you would like to tell fans? Come to the show, because as disappointing as this might sound, it’s not all sax. I’ve got a lot of great musicians you will see. We play our music and some great jazz tunes that people will really get into. We love to play our shows and I guarantee you that every show is played like we’re performing at Carnegie Hall with our career on the line. That’s exactly how we play every night. You will be wowed. GS25, a convenience store run by GS Retail, has started commercializing new food trends that are showing signs of spreading on social network services (SNS) using artificial intelligence (AI). The product development period was cut in half by finding initial signals with AI, breaking away from the existing method of releasing products after the trend began in earnest. GS25 announced on the 17th that it will release "Cheese Seaweed Soup" and "Curry Dangmyeon" using popular recipes on SNS on the 18th. Cheese seaweed soup was conceived from an SNS recipe where cheddar cheese and pepper are added to seaweed soup. Cheese was added to the seaweed soup broth to give it a rich flavor and reduce the greasyness with pure pepper. Curry noodles commercialized a combination of curry with glass noodles instead of rice. It reflects the recent consumption trend of people in their teens and 30s who prefer the chewy texture of noodles and noodles. The curry was cooked to imbue the glass and cheddar cheese was added to preserve the thick texture. GS25's own AI trend analysis system was used to develop the product. It is a method of capturing "trend weak signals" that have not yet been popularized by analyzing consumer reactions and keyword mentions in major domestic search portals, SNS, and online communities. Product planners (MDs) decide whether to actually develop products based on data found by AI. The speed of product development has also accelerated due to the use of AI. Cheese seaweed soup and curry noodles took less than a month and a half to launch after capturing early trends. Considering that it usually takes about three months to develop new convenience store products, the development period has been cut in half. GS25 is expanding its use of AI to the product planning stage to cope with the SNS food trend that has shortened the fashion cycle. In the past, certain combinations or menus were popular at a certain level and then started to develop products, but recently, it is based on the judgment that how quickly the initial signal is captured before the trend begins in earnest determines product competitiveness. The price of the new product is 3,900 won each. GS Ventures Hosts '2026 Tech Day'
GS Group to Build AI Data Center Technology Ecosystem With Startups "Innovative technologies from startups can offer clues to resolving the technical bottlenecks in artificial intelligence data centers. GS Group wants to broaden its points of contact with startups and grow Korea's AI data center technology ecosystem together with them." GS Group Chairman Huh Tae-soo made the remarks on the 15th at the "2026 GS Ventures Tech Day" held at GS Tower in Seoul's Gangnam district. The event was designed to strengthen the competitiveness of the group's value chain by linking innovative startup technologies to its AI data center business, which GS has identified as a new growth engine. A total of seven startups, including six backed by GS Ventures, presented related technologies and explored opportunities to work with group affiliates. GS Group has been identifying and investing in startups across a range of fields through GS Ventures, including power and energy, semiconductors and memory, cooling, and cloud computing. The event was arranged to combine the network and investment experience the group has accumulated with its operational capabilities to find new opportunities in AI data centers. Attendees included Huh and other senior executives, officials from affiliates such as GS Energy, GS Caltex, GS E&C, GS E&R and GS Global (001250.KS), and representatives of the participating startups. Huh expects cooperation with startups holding innovative technologies to generate synergies as the group ramps up its AI data center business. GS Group is pursuing the business to meet surging demand for AI infrastructure. Starting in 2028, it plans to complete a 1.2-gigawatt data center in Donghae, Gangwon Province, in phases, then add another 1.2 gigawatts for a total of 2.4 gigawatts. The plan is to pool the group's capabilities in power generation, construction and large-scale infrastructure operation to deliver stability, efficiency and scalability befitting a world-class facility. The companies at Tech Day unveiled new technologies spanning key areas of the AI data center value chain. In power, Synergy presented a solution to improve the stability of power supply and energy efficiency at AI data centers. Vinssen introduced a hydrogen fuel cell solution for data centers based on technology accumulated in the shipbuilding and shipping sectors, while Exina presented Compute Express Link (CXL)-based intelligent memory that eases data processing bottlenecks. In cooling, CoolMicro presented a direct-to-chip (D2C) liquid cooling solution that removes heat by attaching a cold plate directly to semiconductors, and SDT unveiled an immersion cooling system that cools servers by submerging them in a dielectric coolant. In operations, Elice Group presented a modular AI data center, and Vessl AI showed graphics processing unit (GPU) cloud technology specialized for AI computing workloads. After the company presentations, GS affiliate business managers and the startups held networking sessions. Do Hyun-soo, chief executive of GS AI Infra, the entity dedicated to the AI data center business, and its working-level staff also took part, discussing the feasibility of applying the technologies and ways to link them to the group's businesses. title: Municipal Fixed Income Update August 2026 - Goldman Sachs Asset Management
content: The municipal bond (muni) market underperformed the Treasury market in August, as an extraordinary volume of supply—the strongest August on record—outweighed robust August reinvestment flows. In addition to the supply story, US Treasuries experienced heightened volatility, driven by Fed Chair Warsh’s hawkishly received Jackson Hole speech, Treasury Secretary Bessent announced long-end yield curve intervention, and escalating Middle East tensions reignited the inflation-risk narrative. A busy primary new issue calendar, tight starting valuations, and increased volatility contributed to muni underperformance for the month. Muni yields rose an average of three basis points (bp) in August. The difference between one-year and 30-year muni yields widened 20 bp to 214 bp, leading to a steeper curve. Muni/US Treasury ratios richened in the front end and cheapened at the long end, finishing August at 64/71/87% for 5/10/30 years. Source: Goldman Sachs Asset Management. Bloomberg.  As of August 31, 2026. Source: Goldman Sachs Asset Management. Bloomberg. As of August 31, 2026. The Bloomberg Muni Index declined 0.23% in August, while the Bloomberg Muni High Yield Index increased by 0.22%. All credit ratings (AAA–BBB) saw negative performance within investment grade munis. Source: Goldman Sachs Asset Management. Bloomberg. As of August 31, 2026. Supply for the rest of the year should remain elevated given continued infrastructure needs and refinancing activity. We expect reinvestment demand to taper off in the fall, but anticipate new money flows to continue given attractive yield entry points. Muni/US Treasury ratios remain near fair value and credit spreads are close to their five-year historical averages. We see the opportunity to lock in attractive absolute yields during the recent interest rate volatility. We anticipate headline-driven volatility to remain present, but a resilient underlying economy and healthy reserve balances continue to put municipalities in a strong position to navigate the path forward. August new issue supply amounted to $59 billion ($56 billion tax-exempt and $3 billion taxable). This was 17% higher than August 2025 volumes and 31% higher than July. Year-to-date, new issue volumes are 2% higher than this time last year. Weekly new issuance volumes in August ranged from $12 billion to $19 billion. Notable deals included $3.1 billion in California GO bonds, $2.7 billion in revenue bonds for Los Angeles International Airport, and $1.5 billion NYC GO bonds. Source: Goldman Sachs Asset Management. The Bond Buyer, Barclays. As of August 31, 2026. August saw positive inflows for all four weeks, totaling $6.3 billion. The strongest demand was during the first and last weeks of the month, posting $1.3 billion and $1.4 billion in inflows, respectively. On average, each week had $1 billion worth of inflows based on weekly reporters' data. Overall, August experienced robust demand across both investment grade and long-duration munis. Year-to-date fund inflows have totaled $69 billion, with the majority of flows into investment grade and long duration munis. Source: Goldman Sachs Asset Management. Refinitiv. As of August 31, 2026. Investment grade and high yield spreads both tightened by 2 bp, finishing August at 85 bp and 169 bp, respectively. Within high yield, the transportation and hospital sectors had the strongest performance, returning 1.02% and 0.63%. GO and airline showed the largest negative returns, down 0.32% and 0.21%, respectively. Source: Goldman Sachs Asset Management, Bloomberg. As of August 31, 2026. title: New Neighborhood Grocery Store St. G’s Bodega Opens on St. Cloud’s East End - KNSI
content: (KNSI) – A new neighborhood grocery store opened its doors Wednesday on St. Cloud’s East End. St. G’s Bodega, at 415 E. St. Germain St., is owned by Marla, Madison and Shaelynn Waseka. Marla Waseka spoke with KNSI News moments after the doors opened and says the owners thought about the people living in the neighborhood when they decided to open there. “A lot of them nearby don’t have a vehicle, so this should be an easy way for them to get their groceries, especially when it’s 40 below or 90 above.” Waseka says the owners have a second group of customers in mind. “Also, we’re targeting a market of people who don’t want to go all the way to the back end of a great big store to get a gallon of milk, and so this is easy in and out.” The shelves are stocked with everyday basics like bread, eggs, milk and butter, along with snacks, meal ingredients, personal care items, household goods and tobacco products. Waseka says the inventory will grow over time. The cooler also holds sandwiches and drinks, and there are four tables by the front window for customers who want to stay and eat. The word “bodega” is usually tied to small shops in New York City, and Waseka says that’s the model the owners are following. “It’s a small neighborhood store. Also a neighborhood hub where people can come, they can post events, they can hang out for a little while and get what they need.” St. G’s Bodega is open from 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. seven days a week. title: GS Group Taps Startups for AI Data Centers - 조선일보
content: Group partners with startups on power, cooling, memory solutions for AI data centers, showcased at 2026 Tech Day event GS has decided to pursue a plan to extensively utilize domestic startup technologies as it advances its artificial intelligence (AI) data center business. GS will begin constructing a 1.2GW-scale AI data center in Donghae City, Gangwon Province, in 2028, with plans to expand its capacity to 2.4GW. The group will handle power generation, construction, and operations, while adopting a strategy to enhance the competitiveness of the entire ecosystem by partnering with startups for detailed technologies required for data centers—such as power, cooling, memory, and GPU operations—instead of developing them individually. GS Ventures, the corporate venture capital (CVC) of GS Group, held the "2026 GS Ventures Tech Day" themed on AI data centers at GS Tower in Gangnam District, Seoul, on September 15, it announced on September 16. The annual event, which began in 2023, connects promising startups with group affiliates. This year’s theme focused on AI data centers. Huh Tae-soo, GS chairman, and executives from major affiliates, including GS Energy, GS Caltex, and GS Engineering & Construction, all attended. Seven startups, including those invested in by GS Ventures, showcased technologies related to data centers. The startups targeted real-world challenges faced by AI data centers. They introduced technologies such as energy storage systems (ESS) and hydrogen fuel cells for stable power supply, liquid cooling systems to manage heat from high-performance servers, and next-generation memory technologies to accelerate data transfer speeds during AI computations. Modular facilities for rapid data center installation and cloud technologies for efficient GPU management were also presented. GS officials reviewed the applicability of these technologies on-site and decided to proceed with follow-up discussions to verify their feasibility and potential business applications. Chairman Huh Tae-soo stated, “The innovative technologies of startups will be the key to resolving the technical bottlenecks of data centers.”

title: SEC orders G’s Kicks to halt investment solicitation - BusinessWorld - BusinessWorld Online
content: THE Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has ordered G’s Kicks Billard Hall/G’s Kicks to stop allegedly offering unregistered securities through an  investment scheme, citing what it described as prima facie violations of securities laws. FinancialMarkets News In a notice on Tuesday, the corporate regulator said its Enforcement and  Investor Protection Department (EIPD) issued a cease-and-desist order (CDO) against G’s Kicks on Sept. 8, docketed as SEC EIPD CDO Case No. 2026-0013. The SEC said the alleged investment scheme was promoted through Facebook and other social media platforms, messaging applications, and unverified websites. FinancialMarkets News According to the regulator, the scheme offered guaranteed returns of 8% to 10% within 30 days, along with claims of “risk-free”  investments and unusually fast withdrawals. The SEC said it determined that the arrangement constituted an investment contract under the Howey Test because investors allegedly placed money into a common enterprise with the expectation of earning profits primarily from the efforts of others. According to the commission, investors’ funds were allegedly pooled to finance the opening of a new branch of the G’s Kicks shoe business. The investors were not involved in managing the enterprise but were allegedly promised returns based on their investments, the SEC said. The commission said the solicitation of investments through social media constituted a public offering of securities. Investing Under the Securities Regulation Code (SRC), securities may not be offered or sold in the Philippines without an approved registration statement and the required permit. “Based on the Certifications from the commission’s Company Registration and Monitoring Department (CRMD) G’s Kicks Billard Hall/G’s Kicks is not registered with the Commission either as a corporation or as a partnership; has not registered any securities under Section 8 and 12 of the SRC; has not filed an application for the registration of, and/or a license to sell securities; has not been issued any license to sell securities; and is not a registered issuer of mutual funds, exchange traded funds and proprietary/non-proprietary shares or membership certificates and timeshares under Sections 8 and 12 of the SRC,” the order read. The SEC also said the alleged scheme fell within the Financial Products and Services Consumer Protection Act’s provisions on financial fraud, which cover deceptive investment solicitations. Under the order, G’s Kicks and those acting on its behalf were directed to stop offering or selling unregistered securities until the required registrations and licenses are secured. The order also directed the shutdown of internet accounts and other online platforms linked to the transactions and the alleged investment scheme covered by the case. The respondents and their agents were likewise prohibited from conducting transactions involving funds or assets held with depositary banks, or from transferring, disposing of, or conveying assets in which they have an interest, without SEC authorization. — Alexandria Grace C. title: The 2010s Most Comfortable And Reliable Executive Sedan Can Be Yours For Less Than A New Honda Civic - CarBuzz
content: Subscribe to the CarBuzz newsletter to never miss an update Few used-car bargains reward patient shoppers quite like the fourth-generation Lexus GS. As depreciation has done its quiet work, rear- and all-wheel-drive GS 350 models have settled into genuinely attainable territory — making this one of the most compelling value plays in the used luxury sedan market today. But why are we recommending the Lexus GS in particular, when there are plenty of Camrys, RAV4s, and Lexus LS models available in a similar price range? Put simply, this is one of the most comfortable and luxurious sedans ever built. Here's what you need to know. The fourth (and final) generation Lexus GS was launched in 2011 for the 2012 model year, revised for the 2015 model year, and retired after the 2020 model, with iterative updates bringing the final horsepower output to 311 hp — enough to hustle its two-ton frame to 60 mph in around six seconds. If that doesn't sound like the most exciting car in the world to drive, well, that's not exactly what Lexus was going for. In the 2010s, mid-size sedans in the $50,000–$60,000 range that split the difference between luxury and performance were a dime a dozen. With the GS 350, Lexus managed to stand out by following the wisdom laid out in that old Howlin' Wolf tune, "I'm built for comfort, I ain't built for speed." We can sit here and list everything Lexus did to achieve that end. We can talk about the all-aluminum suspension system, the rear-wheel steering system, and the adjustable dampers, but it really comes down to the experience of driving it. For that, we'll go to our resident GS superfan, Gerhard Horn. "Lexus made F Sport versions of the GS, but I honestly don't know why. This car was unashamedly all about comfort, and all the better for it. The Germans always want to provide sporty handling, which is great on a twisty mountain road, but let's get real for a second. Most of your time spent in a car is in less-than-ideal conditions, like traffic. If that's the case, you just want a comfortable seat, a brilliant sound system, and enough sound insulation to drown out the cries of the poor. The GS does all of the above beautifully." When it was brand new, the Lexus GS 350 delivered millionaire-car refinement on a middle-class budget. Now that prices have fallen sharply, it's closer to millionaire-car refinement on a college-kid's budget. The fourth-generation Lexus GS (L10 platform, spanning model years 2013 to 2020, launched in 2012) has established a remarkably resilient standard in the pre-owned luxury market. Valued for combining Japanese mechanical reliability with refined mid-size luxury, used prices generally span from $12,000 to $24,000 depending on the specific model year, mileage, and trim level. Early pre-facelift models (2013–2015) typically range between $12,000 and $18,000. These early GS 350 and GS 450h hybrids represent some of the strongest value propositions, offering a bulletproof naturally aspirated 3.5-liter V6 and premium cabin materials at a fraction of their original sticker price. That's basically the same as a Honda Civic. For updated 2016 and 2017 models—which introduced aggressive refreshed exterior styling, standard Lexus Safety System+, and the turbocharged four-cylinder GS 200t/300 variant—values command a premium, ranging from $18,000 to $24,000+. Across all model years, the desirable F Sport package and low-mileage examples consistently sit at the higher end of the pricing spectrum. We would never advise buying a used car sight unseen. You need to kick the tires, take it for a test drive, and pop the hood for a good look. But when you go to check out your new-to-you Lexus, don't be surprised if you find absolutely nothing seriously wrong with it. Annual maintenance costs for the GS 350 are remarkably low for a luxury sedan, based on data from RepairPal (annual maintenance estimate) and CarEdge (10-year estimate). In other words, you don't need to lose sleep over cost of ownership. If you can afford to run a Hyundai Elantra or a Honda CR-V, you can afford to drive a Lexus GS. That said, a little preventative maintenance will help ensure you get every mile out of that powertrain that you have coming to you. Beyond all that, just make sure to check the service history. If you don't know when the previous owner last had the oil and filters changed and the tires rotated, it never hurts to get that taken care of a little too soon. And remember: a Lexus is the automotive equivalent of a pet parrot. Take care of it, and you'll have to talk to your estate lawyer someday about who gets it in the will. We want to hear from you. title: Debbie Schaeffer takes her passion for the arts beyond Mrs. G’s - princetoninfo.com
content: Debbie Schaeffer is CEO of Mrs. G’s Appliances in Lawrence Township. Her grandparents, Abe and Beatrice Greenberg, opened a plumbing supply store on East State Street in Trenton in 1935, which evolved into selling refrigerators and other appliances after World War II. As the current face of the business, she is very active in area business association gatherings. Schaeffer is also seen at plays, concerts and even early in the morning at the former Trenton arts festival Art All Night. She supports the arts not only with her pocketbook, but with her presence and promotion. She understands the impact and value of the arts in the community. What first got you involved in arts and culture in the area? My interest in art really started with my mother. Growing up in Yardley, Pennsylvania, she loved museums and galleries and would take us to New Hope to see local artwork. But what really deepened my interest was about 30 years ago, when my children were young and I became involved with the Princeton University Art Museum. I loved the member day trips to places like New York and Philadelphia, where we would visit private homes, artists and collections and really learn about what we were seeing. I loved being with people who were curious about art and the conversations that came with it. At this point in my life, I’m making more time to continue that education. I’ve been taking classes at the Barnes Foundation and recently visited the Yale University Art Gallery, where I learned about the American Revolution through the paintings of John Trumbull. I was fascinated by his story and the history behind the paintings. That’s probably what I enjoy most about art today. You find a work that you love, but then it takes you somewhere else. You start learning about the artist, the history and the world around it. The more I learn, the more curious I become. How do you feel the “power of awe” can influence people in science, arts and culture? I recently attended The Art of Well-Being Annual Summit, presented by Noom at the Princeton University Art Museum, and it really changed the way I think about art and well-being. One of the ideas that stayed with me was that cultural experiences may someday be viewed as an important part of our well-being, much like physical activity is today. I spend a lot of time on my physical health. I play tennis, walk and lift weights, but I’ve come to realize that engaging with art can be another part of taking care of ourselves. Years ago, I fell in love with a Toulouse-Lautrec work at the Barnes and bought a reproduction. It has hung in my living room for more than 10 years, and I still stop and look at it. It creates that little moment of awe. I’ve also changed the way I visit museums. Instead of trying to see everything, I try to choose a few works, slow down, sit on a bench and really look. You start noticing things you didn’t see at first. And you don’t even need to be in a museum. Put a piece of art you love somewhere you’ll see it, or pull one up on your phone instead of checking email or Instagram, and spend a few minutes with it. In a world that rewards being busy, art reminds us to pause. Please tell us about your involvement with the Princeton Symphony. I currently serve on the board of the Princeton Symphony Orchestra and attend most of the performances throughout the year. I absolutely love the orchestra and think we are incredibly fortunate to have it here in Princeton. Rossen Milanov is an amazing conductor, and the musicians are extraordinary. But I have to say, I am especially in love with the Princeton Festival. For several weeks every June, there is something happening almost every day: symphonic music, opera, dance, Broadway, popular music and wonderful guest performers. It’s such a gem, and I would love to see more people from outside Princeton discover it and make it a destination. And one of the things I particularly admire is Princeton Symphony Orchestra BRAVO!, which brings music education to thousands of schoolchildren in our community. Introducing children to live music at a young age is so important. You never know what experience is going to spark a lifelong love of the arts. What fights or struggles do you see locally for the artists you know and the events you frequent? I think one of the biggest struggles is simply getting people to show up. We have wonderful arts organizations, museums, performances and events in this area, but there are so many things competing for everyone’s time and attention. And funding is always an issue. I think local businesses and individuals have a responsibility to support these organizations, not just financially, but by attending, talking about them and introducing other people to them. If we want a vibrant community, the arts have to be part of it. Do you incorporate artistic aspects into the store? Do you keep décor in mind? Absolutely. When we designed the showroom, I wanted it to feel bright, airy and open, almost more like a gallery than a store. We have high ceilings, wide aisles, light colors and beautiful displays that give people room to explore and imagine. I recently read about a University of Minnesota study on how ceiling height can actually influence the way we think. Higher ceilings can encourage more open, creative thinking, while lower ceilings can encourage greater focus. I found that fascinating because, without really knowing the science behind it, we had designed Mrs. G’s that way. You enter through this large, open space where you can imagine the possibilities, and then as you move through the showroom, the spaces become more intimate and the conversations and decisions become more focused. I also believe in engaging all five senses. There are beautiful appliances to see and touch, music playing and, very often, cookies baking, a chef demonstration or even smash burgers on a grill. Have you hosted art events among the many events at Mrs. G’s? Absolutely. I’ve always loved using Mrs. G’s as a gathering place for the arts. For the past two years, we’ve hosted a dinner for Princeton Symphony members that included a live performance, in collaboration with Café Appliances. We’ve also worked with Artworks Trenton and artists like Leon Rainbow, who has become a good friend over the years. One of my favorite projects was our “Paint Our Refrigerators Pink” event to support YWCA breast cancer awareness. We brought graffiti artists and survivors together to paint refrigerators incorporating the pink ribbon. It was creative, colorful and so much fun. Leon’s refrigerator is currently being raffled off. See YWCA Princeton for more details. I’ve also hosted Trenton artists at Mrs. G’s during a Chamber of Commerce event, which gave us an opportunity to introduce the artists and their work to the business community. I love bringing together people who might not otherwise meet: artists, musicians, businesspeople, children and our customers. Art doesn’t always have to be experienced in a museum or gallery. Sometimes the most interesting experiences happen in unexpected places, even an appliance store. What are some of your favorite area arts and culture venues for a night out? I must laugh at the “night out” part because I’m a very early riser! I’ve discovered that I enjoy many of my favorite cultural experiences during the day. The Princeton University Art Museum is certainly at the top of my list. I love going back again and again, especially for the lectures and educational programs. I also love the Sunday afternoon Princeton Symphony performances and McCarter Theatre, where I often choose a matinee. Grounds For Sculpture in Hamilton is truly a gem, and I’m always surprised by how many people who live locally have never been there. It’s such a special combination of art, beautiful landscaping and nature, and I love experiencing it in different seasons because the sculptures and grounds take on an entirely different character. It’s also a wonderful place to walk, relax and exercise both your body and your mind. And having Rat’s Restaurant right there makes the experience even more special. I have a real soft spot for the Bucks County Playhouse in New Hope because I grew up going there, and I still love their productions. And movies are definitely art to me. I’m a big movie fan and love going to the Princeton Garden Theatre, especially for films you might not see everywhere else. I also collect vintage movie posters, particularly Polish movie posters, which I think are incredible works of graphic art. For me, a great cultural experience can be a museum, live music, theater or a wonderful film. We’re incredibly fortunate to have all of that right here in our area. With your engineering and construction background, how do you think the arts can help young people learn about science, history and the world around them? I’m an engineer and have a construction management background, so I certainly value science and hands-on learning. But one thing I’ve come to appreciate increasingly is how the arts can open the door to so many other subjects for young people. Art is an incredible way to learn history. Look at a portrait or a painting of a war, a religious scene, a home or everyday life, and suddenly you start asking questions: Who are these people? What was happening at that time? How did they live? I recently experienced that myself at Yale, learning about the American Revolution through the paintings of John Trumbull. It made the history come alive. We’re also fortunate to have organizations like the Arts Council of Princeton, which offers classes, exhibitions and programs for children as well as adults. I took my own children to museums and exposed them to art, but looking back, I wish I had done even more to connect the art they were seeing to history, science and the world around them. That’s something I’m really looking forward to doing someday with my grandchildren. Do you think supporting the arts is a good fit for chambers of commerce and professional organizations? Yes. I believe supporting the arts is a natural fit for businesses, chambers of commerce and professional associations because supporting the arts is really about supporting the community. The arts bring people together, encourage creativity and lifelong learning, and contribute to a vibrant community where people want to live, work and do business. When businesses support the arts, they’re investing in the overall strength and quality of life of their community. What changes have you seen at arts organizations such as Artworks Trenton and the Arts Council of Princeton over the years? I think one of the biggest changes I’ve seen is how strong and sustainable these organizations have become. The Arts Council of Princeton has wonderful leadership under Adam Welch, a passionate team and strong community support, and continues to offer programs and classes that people really want. Artworks Trenton also has great leadership, and I especially love what they’re doing with young people. Mrs. G’s supported transportation this summer so children in their art programs could visit the Princeton University Art Museum and participate in other experiences outside Trenton. I miss Art All Night, but Artworks continues to create opportunities for artists to be seen and recognized. Both organizations have really become important anchors in their communities. Has supporting and advocating for the arts been part of your family, and is it present in the next generation? Yes, I think it started with my mother. She loved museums and took us to museums, while my grandmother worked all the time and really didn’t have those opportunities. I feel like I’ve taken that interest to another level as I’ve learned more about art history, the power of awe and how experiencing art can contribute to our well-being. I’ve tried to pass that appreciation on to my daughters. Recently, I visited my daughter in San Francisco, and we spent the day at the Legion of Honor. We had so much fun finding the art that resonated with each of us and especially discovering the pieces we loved together. And it’s not only the art. It’s the architecture, the sculpture, the landscape and the entire experience. What is on the horizon? What do you have coming up? One project I’m particularly excited about is our partnership with Electrolux Group and HomeWorks Trenton, a nonprofit boarding school for girls in Trenton. Electrolux Group is donating new kitchen and laundry appliances, with Mrs. G’s coordinating the delivery and installation. One of the new ranges even specializes in making pizza. Antonio Carannante, owner of Brother’s Pizza and Blend Bistro, and I are planning to spend an evening with the girls teaching them the art of making the perfect pizza. It’s another fun way to bring creativity, learning and community together. Mrs. G Appliances, is located at 2720 U.S. 1 Business, Lawrence Township, New Jersey 08648. title:
Surily G’s Opal brings Art Deco
details and pastels to contemporary occasion wear - IndulgExpress
content: A fragment of Art Deco finds its way into the wardrobe through delicate cutwork, mirror work and luminous textures. This is Opal, the first chapter of Surily G by designer Surily DP Goel’s Modern Heirlooms 2026 — a fivepart collection that will unfold through monthly launches. “I wanted to explore the different moods that come with celebration dressing, rather than put everything into one collection or one aesthetic. The five chapters allow that story to unfold gradually,” Surily begins. Opal introduces a softer expression of Indian occasion wear, with lehengas, saris and shararas designed for intimate wedding celebrations, festive soirées and modern occasions. The collection also includes an embroidered flowy kaftan, a kurta with flared pants and dupatta, a kurta with straight pants and dupatta, an embroidered tube blouse with a draped skirt, an embroidered belt with a long jacket and a blouse with a cape and skirt. “With Opal, I wanted to explore a softer, more understated side of celebration dressing. I was drawn to the idea of working with light, texture and femininity and seeing how techniques like mirror work and cutwork could be interpreted in a way that feels fresh and relevant. That naturally led to the ethereal pastels, luminous textures and delicate tulle that you see throughout the collection. I chose this name because of the way an opal stone plays with the light; opals have this beautiful luminescent quality, which I wanted to bring to this collection,” the designer tells us. Opal takes its cues from a softer palette. At the same time, its reflective details lend the collection a sense of travel, bringing to mind resort evenings where occasion dressing can move easily from a destination wedding to a festive dinner. “The palette plays a big role in creating that mood, moving through soft blush and powder pinks, delicate peach and champagne tones, with touches of aqua and turquoise that bring a fresher contrast to the softer shades,” she shares. There are 18 outfits in the edit, spanning three key silhouette categories. Alongside the more traditional occasion-wear forms, the collection plays with fluid separates and layered dressing, while Art Deco-inspired cutwork brings a graphic edge to the otherwise delicate palette. Mirror work catches the light, reinforcing the collection’s connection to the gemstone that gives it its name. “For this edit, I focused on creating a versatile selection of occasion silhouettes that can work across different kinds of celebrations. The craftsmanship adds another dimension through shimmering mirror work and intricate Art Deco-inspired cutwork. I am really drawn to the structure and glamour of Art Deco, especially its strong geometric language. We translated that into the collection through geometric motifs, cutwork and mirror embroidery. I love the contrast between sharp, graphic detailing and these very fluid, delicate silhouettes that you’ll find in Opal,” she reveals. Among the edit, the designer points to pieces that bring a more contemporary take to festive dressing. “We always love a sharara, so the Aqua Sharara that we have with this very chic, contemporary choli is a great piece for the festive season. I also love the Nude Lehenga, which features this pastel multicoloured embroidery. It’s both sophisticated and playful,” she explains. As the opening chapter of Modern Heirlooms, Opal sets the tone for what follows, balancing Indian occasion-wear silhouettes with lighter textures, reflective craftsmanship and a palette that lends itself to intimate celebrations as much as destination dressing. With four more chapters still to unfold through monthly launches, the collection leaves room for the story to move through different moods and occasions. “Opal is the beginning of the Modern Heirlooms story by setting the tone with a softer approach to occasion dressing. As the collection unfolds, the focus will shift towards different kinds of celebrations, moving from more intimate moments to destination weddings and, eventually, more glamorous occasions. Kim Do-young (56), former director of GS Construction, took office as the new head of the Jeju Special Self-Governing Province Development Corporation, which makes Jeju Samdasoo. President Kim, who has 27 years of experience in sales, exports, construction, and new businesses in private companies, presented a blueprint to increase the competitiveness of Jeju Samdasoo and innovate the management of the corporation by using the "second start-up spirit." The Jeju Development Corporation announced that President Kim received a letter of appointment from Jeju Governor Wi Sung-gon on the 16th and began his official work as the 13th president. In the afternoon of this day, he held an inauguration ceremony at Samdasoo Plant and announced five key management directions. President Kim said at the inauguration ceremony, "We cannot go any further by relying on the success equation of the past," adding, "Let's start again with a second entrepreneurial spirit by reviving the passion and challenge consciousness that created something out of nothing for the residents in the early days of the construction." The management direction proposed by President Kim is △Sustainable growth based on the spirit of the second start-up △Fostering talent and fair performance compensation △Detailed management centered on the field △Communication and transparent management △Balance of profitability and publicity. In order to strengthen the competitiveness of Jeju Samdasoo, a core business, we will speed up distribution and sales innovation. It plans to advance its distribution network and advance its distribution policy, while establishing a sales system for each target and channel. Based on smart production and eco-friendly innovation, it is also expanding the global market beyond the domestic market. In the operation of the organization, it plans to increase the professionalism of executives and employees and establish a compensation system based on performance. A preemptive safety management system will be established and quality control will be strengthened with the aim of "zero" workplace safety accidents. President Kim graduated from Oh Hyun High School and obtained a bachelor's and master's degree from the Department of Business Administration at Seoul National University. From LG Uplus to GS E&C managing director, he has been in charge of sales, exports, construction, and new business discovery in private companies. It has built up its overall management capabilities by experiencing strategic planning, new business discovery, and data-based distribution management in large organizations. Earlier, the Jeju Provincial Council's Environmental City Committee held a confirmation hearing on the 15th and presented a qualified opinion after verifying President Kim's morality, expertise, and job performance ability. Kim said he would balance profitability and publicity by combining his experiences in private companies with the roles and responsibilities of public companies. "Performance comes from implementation, not slogans, and executives and employees are always at the center of the implementation," he said. "I will lead by example first, execute all tasks thoroughly, and play with you."
